obligations.obligation: 1. EXACTNESS: bitwise uint32 parallel==serial per-arm AND cross-arm; block grid identical to the serial loop's
obligations.finding: All comparisons go through outputs_bitwise_equal -> np.array_equal(u32(a), u32(b)) with u32 = ascontiguousarray().view(np.uint32) (region_case.py:88-93) -- bitwise on raw float32 bits, frozen-suite convention. A-arm: 11 shapes x budgets {1,2,4} x seeds {0,1} = 66 cases assert serial==parallel AND parallel==whole-call oracle (test_region_composition.py:31-58). B-arm: serial==parallel==whole lw_primary_b call, plus report.max_in_flight==1 (:61-92). C-arm: serial==parallel==whole NativeHandle.execute over 3 shapes incl. tail 257 (:105-137). Cross-arm A==B, A==C on one adversarial case through the same boundary (:140-160); repeated-execution stability on one pool over 4 runs (:163-177). Block-grid identity is structural, not just tested: block_spans() is literally the serial loop expression (region_plan.py:88-90); regions are pure block-INDEX ranges over total_blocks=ceil(n/b) (:99-105) and never touch pixels; both executors build spans exclusively via plan.block_spans() (region_pool.py:604-606, 919-921), so no other span source exists. Pinned by property tests over 8 (total,b) grids incl. b=7 and edges 0/1/127/128/129 (test_region_plan.py:23-30) and gapless ascending exact partition with region edges subset of block edges (:33-54). Zero skips in both reruns: the native C-arm genuinely executed.

obligations.obligation: 2. THREAD BUDGET: runtime-observed in-flight <= N for BLOCK_FANOUT; in-flight==1 + quiescence for SELF_PARALLEL; no second-pool budget blowup
obligations.finding: Observed, not configured: max_in_flight is maintained under the pool lock around real block execution, incremented before slot acquire and decremented after release (region_pool.py:402-404, 424-425), and reported per call. test_max_in_flight_never_exceeds_budget asserts <= N and >= 2 for N>=2 with a GIL-releasing sleep forcing genuine overlap (test_region_pool_budget.py:37-52); a live thread census taken INSIDE blocks bounds threading.active_count() to baseline+N-1 (:55-76); N=1 spawns zero threads with in_flight==1 (:79-90). Workers spawned: exactly N-1, lazily, once (region_pool.py:521-536); the submitting thread works the same queue (run(), :436-451), so executing threads <= N by construction; slots are also N (_SlotPool(budget), :475). SELF_PARALLEL: a plain sequential for-loop leasing one slot at a time (region_pool.py:653-688) -- in-flight==1 structurally; nothing is ever enqueued, so pre-existing workers stay blocked on queue.get() (quiescent); asserted with the real numba kernel (test_region_composition.py:90) and workers==0 on a fresh pool (test_region_pool_budget.py:93-108); reviewer probe additionally confirmed in-flight==1 and zero worker spawns on a pool with LIVE workers from a prior fanout session (the previously untested case). No overlap path between the modes: sessions are exclusive (PoolSessionConflict at region_pool.py:573-586) and re-entry from inside a block hits the same guard (:111-127); a concurrent second submission is refused under an actively held session (:130-162). Numba layer sizing to the same N is test-wiring (conftest.py:41-42 LW_TEST_THREADS used for both set_num_threads and RegionPool) -- an integrator contract, honestly documented (docstring :39-45). Second-pool paths: shared_pool() is keyed (pid,budget), hard-capped at 8 distinct live budgets with loud PoolRegistryBound, closed/poisoned entries replaced in place (region_pool.py:812-837; test :165-192). Notes N2/N3 below record the two declarative/per-owner residuals.

obligations.obligation: 3. CANCELLATION: defined first-error order, no partial results as success, native failure stays loud, pool reusable after cancel
obligations.finding: First-error order is DEFINED (lowest ADMITTED block index; _raise_first, region_pool.py:710-743) and proven immune to wall-clock inversion: block 7 fails immediately, block 2 fails 250 ms later, block 2's error is raised (test_region_cancellation.py:61-88). The original exception object is re-raised with type intact: KeyError identity (:29-44), UnsupportedInput stays a TypeError so the dispatcher's fallback decision is unchanged (:91-105), NativeExecutionError never swallowed or converted (:108-119) -- including a synthetic post-launch failure through the REAL handle wrapper (test_region_consumers.py:179-209). No starts after cancel and nothing past the failing block starts, under a barrier-held in-flight scenario (:122-164). No report is returned and nothing is published as success on failure -- the raise happens before RegionReport construction (region_pool.py:628-630, 638-640); structural output checks run before any dispatch (:203-220; execute validates at :597-599). Drain is bounded (all queued items are dequeued and retired exactly once; run() loops until outstanding==0, :436-451). Pool reusable after a cancelled session: state is reset in finally blocks (:618-623, 587-591) and a reviewer probe ran a clean bitwise-correct session on the same pool after a cancelled one -- no dedicated in-suite test (note N5, R2). Note N1 records the theoretical multi-failure divergence corner.

obligations.obligation: 4. SCRATCH: alias/mutation safety, dispatch-size independence, boundedness
obligations.finding: Dispatch-size independence incl. region_blocks=10**6: identical bits and allocation count == min(budget, blocks-per-region) regardless of region count (test_region_scratch.py:59-74); bounded by slots not blocks: 32 blocks in one region -> exactly 4 allocations at budget 4 (:77-83). Alias safety: byte-extent disjointness of concurrently leased slots plus same-object reuse across leases (:86-96); two simultaneously-leased distinct slots OBSERVED under a barrier (:99-122). Reuse invisibility: NaN-poisoning every slot buffer between runs changes nothing, and the canary has teeth -- a read-before-write consumer detects the poison (:125-172). Fixed-shape arenas: full-capacity lease + [:rows] tail view (consumers.py:88-91, region_pool.py:224-227); shape/dtype rebinding rejected loudly with ScratchShapeError, and a misbinding consumer's tail block fails with that type through the region (:175-203). Slots == budget, one exclusive free-list lease per executing block (region_pool.py:303-345, 408-423).

obligations.obligation: 5. FORK HOOK: strictly lock-free after_in_child; fork-while-active exercised; no constructed-pool escape
obligations.finding: The hook body (_poison_child_pools, region_pool.py:865-878) was inspected statement-by-statement: a global int increment (_FORK_GENERATION += 1), _POOLS.clear() (dict clear), a per-pool plain attribute write (pool._poisoned = True), _LIVE_POOLS.clear() (list clear). No with, no .acquire, no lock construction or use; RegionPool defines no __slots__/__setattr__ override and no descriptor shadows _poisoned (the read-only `poisoned` property intercepts only its own name), so the write is a plain instance-dict store. The hook never touches queues, slots or worker state, and a poisoned pool is refused service at both _ensure_workers and _session_guard (:524-529, 575-578). Escape analysis: the hook is registered at module import (:881-882) and EVERY RegionPool registers itself inside __init__ via _track_pool (:477) before the constructor returns, so no pool exists untracked-at-fork except one refused by the 64-pool tracking cap (note N4 -- unreachable via shared_pool's 8-budget cap). Real-fork tests: child use of the inherited pool raises ForkedRegionPool, child re-prepare via the cleared table reproduces the parent's bits bitwise, parent pool unpoisoned and reusable (test_region_fork_policy.py:45-94); fork WHILE a block is held in-flight mid-session: child runs clean on a fresh owner, parent session completes bitwise==serial (:97-171); shared_pool() in the child is a fresh instance with advanced fork generation (:174-208). Children are minimal (pure numpy consumer, os._exit) per the file's own safety note. All 3 DeprecationWarnings in the suite are these os.fork calls, as claimed.

notes: N1 (cancellation corner): with TWO OR MORE failing blocks, a lower-index block can rarely be skipped by cancellation after a higher-index block's error is admitted (dequeue-to-start window in _FanoutSession.handle, region_pool.py:392-406), so the raised error can differ from strict serial's choice in that corner. The defined rule -- lowest ADMITTED index -- is deterministic, tested for wall-clock inversion, and always raises a real admitted error with type intact; the docstring phrase 'exactly the error a serial loop would have raised first' (:91-92) is slightly stronger than what is guaranteed for multi-failure races. Single-failure and all-admitted cases match serial exactly.

N2 (declarative mode): the owner enforces the budget against the DECLARED parallelism class; an internally-parallel consumer misdeclaring BLOCK_FANOUT would exceed N and the owner cannot detect it. Documented honestly in-suite (test_region_consumers.py:106-115); an integrator contract, same class as any thread-safety declaration.

N3 (per-owner, not process-wide): concurrent sessions on two DISTINCT budgets (or two explicit pools) are not mutually excluded and can sum to N1+N2 threads; shared_pool caps distinct budgets at 8 but does not sum-cap. The module docstring acknowledges this ('live threads bounded by sum(N_i-1) over live pools', :80-81); the workflow binding of ONE threads_per_worker per process is the intended guard. Minor related nit: explicit resolve_budget validates <= cpu_count but not the runtime cpu_budget tightening that the None path inherits (:766-784).

N4 (fork-tracking cap is silent): _track_pool (region_pool.py:801-809) prunes closed/poisoned pools at the 64-pool cap and then SILENTLY declines to track further pools; a 65th explicit live RegionPool would escape fork poisoning (its inherited workers do not exist in the child). Unreachable through shared_pool() (8-budget loud cap) and outside every test; inconsistent with the module's own 'misconfiguration must fail loudly' philosophy -- see R1.
N5: no dedicated test for a successful session on the same pool AFTER a cancelled session (structurally reset via finally blocks; reviewer probe confirmed bitwise==serial) -- see R2.
N6: mixed-mode single-pool reuse (fanout session, then SELF_PARALLEL with live workers) is structurally quiescent and reviewer-probe-confirmed but untested in-suite -- see R3.
